- Overestimate prices during sentiment spikes (especially +1.00 or +0.67) — reduce forecast peaks by 20–40%.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00) — add 10–30% buffer to low sentiment periods.
- Avoid long-term overconfidence in 30-day forecasts — cap forecast values at 1.5x recent 18-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Correct for mean reversion: if forecast is >20% above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 15–25% unless sentiment is sustained bullish.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 2–3 days prior) often predicts 1–2 day price correction — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment shifts sharply.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast peaks >30% above prior peak, reduce by 30–50% to avoid overcorrection.
- Use sentiment history to weight forecast decay: if sentiment is mixed (0.33/0.67), apply 15–20% dampening to forecast volatility.
